display_title: [CI] Force full bazel-diff CI runs when external repository definitions or patches change

head_commit.message:
[CI] Force full bazel-diff CI runs when external repository definitions or patches change

On pull requests, `build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` invokes `bazel-diff` with `--excludeExternalTargets` and `--fineGrainedHashExternalRepos=@tsl,@@+tsl_extension+tsl`. Because external repository targets outside `@tsl` are not fine-grained hashed and files consumed by repository rules (`workspace.bzl`, `*.BUILD`, `*.patch`, etc.) are not direct target inputs in `deps(//xla/... + //build_tools/... + @tsl//tsl/...)`, PRs that only modified external repository definitions, overlays, or patches (such as openxla/xla#52165 modifying `third_party/mkl_dnn/{workspace.bzl, mkldnn_v1_async.BUILD, *.patch}`) previously received `Decision=SKIP` and bypassed presubmit test execution.

Extend `GLOBAL_BAZEL_CONFIG_PATTERNS` in `build_tools/ci/change_detector.py` so `is_global_config_changed()` forces a `FULL` test run when files that define, configure, overlay, or patch external repositories are modified:
- Top-level workspace macros (`workspace[0-9]+.bzl`), `MODULE.bazel.lock`, and hermetic pip lockfiles (`requirements_lock_*.txt`).
- External repository definitions (`**/workspace.bzl`), repository helpers (`third_party/{repo,quilt_repo}.bzl`), Bzlmod module extensions (`third_party/extensions/*.bzl`, `third_party/**/*extension.bzl`), and external repo setup/configure/init/redist rules (`third_party/**/*{configure,init_repositor,redist,download,repo,setup}*.bzl`).
- External repository overlay `BUILD` files (`**/*.BUILD`, `**/*.BUILD.bazel`, and `BUILD`/`BUILD.bazel`/`BUILD.system` under `third_party/` external repo directories), patches (`third_party/**/*.{patch,diff}`, `third_party/**/patches/**`, `third_party/**/series`), and templates (`third_party/**/*.tpl`).

To keep incremental target selection targeted, first-party vendored `@tsl` files (`third_party/tsl/tsl/**`) and first-party Python/pywrap build rules (`third_party/py/{numpy,rules_pywrap}/**`, `third_party/rules_python/**`) remain excluded from `GLOBAL_BAZEL_CONFIG_PATTERNS` because they are directly tracked in the `bazel-diff` target graph.

display_title: PR #52061: [XLA:GPU] Only fuse AMAX reductions into cuDNN convolution fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52061: [XLA:GPU] Only fuse AMAX reductions into cuDNN convolution fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52061

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_conv_fusion`, `ConvFusionRewriter` pulls any scalar `reduce` that follows a convolution into the `__cudnn$fusion`, and `CuDnnFusionCompiler` then emits every fused `reduce` as a cuDNN `AMAX` reduction without looking at the reducer or the init value. So `sum(conv(x, w))`, `max(conv(x, w))` and `min(conv(x, w))` all return the maximum absolute value of the convolution output.

This change adds `IsCudnnAmaxReduce` to `cudnn_fusion_utils`, which only accepts the pattern the compiler implements: a scalar f32 `reduce` of `abs(...)` (through bitcasts) with a `maximum` reducer and a zero or `-inf` init. The f32 part matters too: the compiler hard-codes f32 compute for the reduction, and a fused bf16 or f16 amax currently fails to compile with "No valid engine configs". The rewriter uses it to decide whether a reduce can be an epilogue, so any other reduce stays an ordinary XLA reduce outside the fusion. The fusion compiler uses it too and returns `Unimplemented` instead of building an `AMAX` node for a reduce it cannot represent.

Fixes #50470.

## 🎯 Justification

Repro from the issue (f32 NCHW conv followed by `reduce` with `add`), RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120), `run_hlo_module --xla_gpu_experimental_enable_conv_fusion=true`:

```
** Result with reference runner HloRunner **  f32[] 7.82932281
Actual literal:                               f32[] 0.169757605
```

With the flag off the CUDA result matches the interpreter. The same thing happens for `maximum` and `minimum` reducers; all three return the same number as `max(abs(conv))`. The cuDNN graph dump in the issue shows `REDUCTION mode=AMAX` right after `CONV_FPROP`. Turing cards are not affected because epilogue fusion needs Ampere.

The FP8 recipe that this code was written for (`amax = reduce(abs(conv), -inf), to_apply=max`) still fuses, which the new unit and compiler tests check. Other reductions were producing wrong values before, so there is nothing to regress; they now run in XLA's own reduction emitter, the same as with the flag off.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`//xla/backends/gpu/transforms:conv_fusion_rewriter_test` - new `SumReduceEpilogueNotFused`, `MaxReduceWithoutAbsNotFused`, `AmaxReduceWithPositiveInitNotFused`, `AmaxReduceBf16NotFused` (reduce stays outside the fusion) and `AmaxReduceFused` (the FP8 amax pattern is still fused). The negative tests fail before the fix.

`//xla/backends/gpu/transforms:cudnn_fusion_compiler_test` - new `GetAvailablePlanCountRejectsNonAmaxReduce` (an `add` reduce in a hand-written `__cudnn$fusion` is rejected with `Unimplemented`, fails before the fix) and `GetAvailablePlanCountFromConvolutionFusionWithAmax` (conv + amax still gets a plan).

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

`//xla/backends/gpu/transforms:conv_fusion_rewriter_test` - new `ScalarReduceEpiloguesAfterConv` runs `sum`, `max` and `min` of a convolution with the flag on against the interpreter with constant inputs (`x = -1`, `w = 1`, every conv output is -18). Fails before the fix (GPU returns 18 for all three). Needs 1 GPU (Ampere+).

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

head_commit.message:
Verify that all processes compiled the same executable

If the processes of a multi-process run compile different executables, they can issue collectives in a different order and hang until some timeout kicks in. One way to get there is autotuning with `--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false`, since then each process autotunes on its own and can end up with a different schedule.

So this change makes `FunctionalHloRunner::Compile` publish the fingerprint of the compiled executable in the key-value store and compare it with the fingerprints of all other processes. If they differ, compilation fails with a `FailedPrecondition` error that lists which processes compiled which fingerprint. The check only runs if the compile options contain a key-value store and more than one process.

The fingerprint covers the optimized HLO including the schedule, but not backend configs. So it catches a different order of collectives, but not every difference in the autotuning results. (For GPU the fingerprint gets computed during compilation anyway, so the check is cheap.)

The check is on by default, which means that runs where the processes compiled different executables but happened not to hang will fail now too. I think that's the better default since the processes don't run the same program in that case. The check can be disabled with `PreprocessingOptions::verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` or the `--verify_executable_fingerprint_across_processes` flag of `//xla/tools/multihost_hlo_runner:hlo_runner_main`.

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

display_title: xla(gpu): Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry and wire CommandBufferThunk

head_commit.message:
xla(gpu): Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry and wire CommandBufferThunk

Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry (default false).
CommandBufferConversionPass builds CommandBufferThunkOptions from
DebugOptions and passes them to CommandBufferThunk, which opens
ScopedCommandBufferAnnotation::Root around command buffer recording (including
updates and graph finalization) only if its command buffer
SupportsNodeAnnotations() (CUDA 13.2+ toolkit, runtime and driver); otherwise
the flag is ignored with a one-time warning. The root carries the module's
top-level annotation. The version decision lives in the CUDA backend, so the
backend-neutral pass and thunk do not depend on stream_executor/cuda.

CommandExecutor pushes one ScopedCommandBufferAnnotation per command with the
lazy constructor, so the per-command annotation string
(GetInstructionAnnotationString, sharing GetInstructionAnnotation's lookup) is
only built while recording is on. Adds GetCurrentModuleAnnotations() to
annotation.h.

display_title: Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

head_commit.message:
Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

While most XLA GitHub Actions CI jobs in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` already use `bazel-diff` with `cquery` to filter presubmit runs to impacted targets, `XLA_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_ONEAPI_GITHUB_ACTIONS` still run full builds on every PR. (`XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_HERMETIC_ROCM_GITHUB_ACTIONS` is intentionally left without `bazel-diff` because the 2x `cquery` overhead exceeds the savings on that build-only job.)

So this change enables `use_bazel_diff=True` (`bazel_diff_use_cquery=True`) for Windows CPU and oneAPI, and tightens how `xla/build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` invokes `bazel-diff` across all jobs:

1. Passes `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope` in `get_cquery_command_options`, constructs `--cqueryExpression` from `build.target_patterns`, and excludes `-//xla/stream_executor/sycl/...` on Windows so `bazel cquery` only analyzes each job's in-scope targets.
2. Passes `--excludeExternalTargets` (and `--bazelStartupOptions` to `get-impacted-targets`) so `bazel-diff` does not spawn a second Bazel server to run `bazel mod graph` or query `//external:all-targets`.
3. Writes only the already-filtered explicit targets to `filtered_impacted_targets.txt` without re-appending negative directory wildcards (`-//xla/backends/gpu/...`, `-//xla/service/gpu/...`, `-//xla/tpu/...`), avoiding loading excluded packages during `bazel build --target_pattern_file`.

Measured improvements on PR #51454 (CI scripts change) and PR #51508 (C++ CPU + GPU change) compared to baseline PR runs:

- `XLA Windows x86 CPU`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 6,752 Windows CPU targets (instead of failing on excluded SYCL/GPU packages across 34,676 targets) and builds only impacted targets (59 actions on PR #51454 and 4,742 actions on PR #51508, instead of 42,496 actions for a full 6,570-target build).
  - Cuts `bazel-diff get-impacted-targets` from **2m15s** to **2.1s** (by avoiding a second Bazel server) and `bazel build --target_pattern_file` on a 12-target change from **2m54s** to **14.3s** (reducing total `build.py` time from **10m56s** to **6m10s**).
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 679 oneAPI targets (`100.6s` at base, `4.2s` at head) and skips the 34,652-action build when no oneAPI targets are impacted (**2m32s** in `bazel-diff` with `Decision=SKIP`).
- Existing Linux `bazel-diff` jobs (from scoping `cquery` via `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope`):
  - Prevents GPU C++ changes from falsely marking ~1,020 GPU targets as `IMPACTED` on CPU jobs (on PR #51508, editing `dot_search_space.cc` impacted 3,474 targets on `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`, 0 GPU targets on the CPU jobs, and only the 1 modified CPU test).
  - `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`: `cquery` target count drops from **33,876** to **3,948** (**88% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **321s-329s** to **177.6s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,685** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **233s-253s** to **133.9s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux ARM64 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,669** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **270s-463s** to **131.3s** (**51%+ faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,582** to **8,683** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **274.5s** to **157.5s** (**43% faster**).

display_title: PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

head_commit.message:
PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49580

📝 Summary of Changes
#ai_generated (but it's been in use internally for several weeks)

When XLA:CPU reduces a large array, it first splits the reduction into a reduce-window that produces partial sums and a smaller reduce over those. The fusion pass knows how to *fuse producers into a reduce*, but not into a *reduce-window*. So in something like `sum(x * y)`, the multiply generates its own loop and writes its entire result to memory, which is read immediately after by the reduce (instead of performing a more optimal loop fusion).

The actual fix is adding `kReduceWindow` to `CanBeLoopFused`, which is one line. I also had to teach `ReusesOperandElements` that a reduce-window with non-overlapping windows touches each input element only once, *as is already done for reduce*.

🎯 Justification

This affects every large reduction that doesn't go to YNNPACK. I ran into it while looking into #49131.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

```
ENTRY main {
  x = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(0)
  y = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(1)
  m = bf16[64,1048576] multiply(x, y)
  c = bf16[] constant(0)
  ROOT r = bf16[64] reduce(m, c), dimensions={1}, to_apply=add
}
```

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| bf16 (above) | 78.0 ms | 28.8 ms |
| same in s32 | 77.7 ms | 12.7 ms |

I didn't see any changes outside the noise on the other CPU benchmarks.

🧪 Unit Tests:

New tests in `hlo_instruction_test` check that a reduce-window reuses elements only when its windows overlap. In `cpu_instruction_fusion_test`, one test fuses a multiply into a non-overlapping reduce-window and another checks that `exp` stays out of an overlapping one.

There was also an existing test in `cpu_fusion_test` that used reduce-window as its example of an op that can't be fused, which is no longer true, so I switched it to sort.

TreeReductionRewriter splits large reductions into a reduce-window followed
by a reduce. CanBeLoopFused did not accept kReduceWindow, so the input of the
reduce-window was materialized.

Add kReduceWindow to CanBeLoopFused. Make ReusesOperandElements return false
for the array operands of a reduce-window with non-overlapping, undilated
windows, as it already does for kReduce.

Merging this change closes #49580

head_commit.message:
PR #52061: [XLA:GPU] Only fuse AMAX reductions into cuDNN convolution fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52061

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_conv_fusion`, `ConvFusionRewriter` pulls any scalar `reduce` that follows a convolution into the `__cudnn$fusion`, and `CuDnnFusionCompiler` then emits every fused `reduce` as a cuDNN `AMAX` reduction without looking at the reducer or the init value. So `sum(conv(x, w))`, `max(conv(x, w))` and `min(conv(x, w))` all return the maximum absolute value of the convolution output.

This change adds `IsCudnnAmaxReduce` to `cudnn_fusion_utils`, which only accepts the pattern the compiler implements: a scalar f32 `reduce` of `abs(...)` (through bitcasts) with a `maximum` reducer and a zero or `-inf` init. The f32 part matters too: the compiler hard-codes f32 compute for the reduction, and a fused bf16 or f16 amax currently fails to compile with "No valid engine configs". The rewriter uses it to decide whether a reduce can be an epilogue, so any other reduce stays an ordinary XLA reduce outside the fusion. The fusion compiler uses it too and returns `Unimplemented` instead of building an `AMAX` node for a reduce it cannot represent.

Fixes #50470.

## 🎯 Justification

Repro from the issue (f32 NCHW conv followed by `reduce` with `add`), RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120), `run_hlo_module --xla_gpu_experimental_enable_conv_fusion=true`:

```
** Result with reference runner HloRunner **  f32[] 7.82932281
Actual literal:                               f32[] 0.169757605
```

With the flag off the CUDA result matches the interpreter. The same thing happens for `maximum` and `minimum` reducers; all three return the same number as `max(abs(conv))`. The cuDNN graph dump in the issue shows `REDUCTION mode=AMAX` right after `CONV_FPROP`. Turing cards are not affected because epilogue fusion needs Ampere.

The FP8 recipe that this code was written for (`amax = reduce(abs(conv), -inf), to_apply=max`) still fuses, which the new unit and compiler tests check. Other reductions were producing wrong values before, so there is nothing to regress; they now run in XLA's own reduction emitter, the same as with the flag off.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`//xla/backends/gpu/transforms:conv_fusion_rewriter_test` - new `SumReduceEpilogueNotFused`, `MaxReduceWithoutAbsNotFused`, `AmaxReduceWithPositiveInitNotFused`, `AmaxReduceBf16NotFused` (reduce stays outside the fusion) and `AmaxReduceFused` (the FP8 amax pattern is still fused). The negative tests fail before the fix.

`//xla/backends/gpu/transforms:cudnn_fusion_compiler_test` - new `GetAvailablePlanCountRejectsNonAmaxReduce` (an `add` reduce in a hand-written `__cudnn$fusion` is rejected with `Unimplemented`, fails before the fix) and `GetAvailablePlanCountFromConvolutionFusionWithAmax` (conv + amax still gets a plan).

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.
Copybara import of the project:

9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

Merging this change closes #48875

display_title: Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

head_commit.message:
Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

While most XLA GitHub Actions CI jobs in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` already use `bazel-diff` with `cquery` to filter presubmit runs to impacted targets, `XLA_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_ONEAPI_GITHUB_ACTIONS` still run full builds on every PR. (`XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_HERMETIC_ROCM_GITHUB_ACTIONS` is intentionally left without `bazel-diff` because the 2x `cquery` overhead exceeds the savings on that build-only job.)

So this change enables `use_bazel_diff=True` (`bazel_diff_use_cquery=True`) for Windows CPU and oneAPI, and tightens how `xla/build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` invokes `bazel-diff` across all jobs:

1. Passes `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope` in `get_cquery_command_options`, constructs `--cqueryExpression` from `build.target_patterns`, and excludes `-//xla/stream_executor/sycl/...` on Windows so `bazel cquery` only analyzes each job's in-scope targets.
2. Passes `--excludeExternalTargets` (and `--bazelStartupOptions` to `get-impacted-targets`) so `bazel-diff` does not spawn a second Bazel server to run `bazel mod graph` or query `//external:all-targets`.
3. Writes only the already-filtered explicit targets to `filtered_impacted_targets.txt` without re-appending negative directory wildcards (`-//xla/backends/gpu/...`, `-//xla/service/gpu/...`, `-//xla/tpu/...`), avoiding loading excluded packages during `bazel build --target_pattern_file`.

Measured improvements on PR #51454 (CI scripts change) and PR #51508 (C++ CPU + GPU change) compared to baseline PR runs:

- `XLA Windows x86 CPU`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 6,752 Windows CPU targets (instead of failing on excluded SYCL/GPU packages across 34,676 targets) and builds only impacted targets (59 actions on PR #51454 and 4,742 actions on PR #51508, instead of 42,496 actions for a full 6,570-target build).
  - Cuts `bazel-diff get-impacted-targets` from **2m15s** to **2.1s** (by avoiding a second Bazel server) and `bazel build --target_pattern_file` on a 12-target change from **2m54s** to **14.3s** (reducing total `build.py` time from **10m56s** to **6m10s**).
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 679 oneAPI targets (`100.6s` at base, `4.2s` at head) and skips the 34,652-action build when no oneAPI targets are impacted (**2m32s** in `bazel-diff` with `Decision=SKIP`).
- Existing Linux `bazel-diff` jobs (from scoping `cquery` via `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope`):
  - Prevents GPU C++ changes from falsely marking ~1,020 GPU targets as `IMPACTED` on CPU jobs (on PR #51508, editing `dot_search_space.cc` impacted 3,474 targets on `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`, 0 GPU targets on the CPU jobs, and only the 1 modified CPU test).
  - `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`: `cquery` target count drops from **33,876** to **3,948** (**88% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **321s-329s** to **177.6s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,685** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **233s-253s** to **133.9s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux ARM64 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,669** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **270s-463s** to **131.3s** (**51%+ faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,582** to **8,683** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **274.5s** to **157.5s** (**43% faster**).

display_title: xla(gpu): Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry and wire CommandBufferThunk

head_commit.message:
xla(gpu): Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry and wire CommandBufferThunk

Add --xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer_telemetry (default false).
CommandBufferConversionPass builds CommandBufferThunkOptions from
DebugOptions and passes them to CommandBufferThunk, which opens
ScopedCommandBufferAnnotation::Root around command buffer recording (including
updates and graph finalization) only if its command buffer
SupportsNodeAnnotations() (CUDA 13.2+ toolkit, runtime and driver); otherwise
the flag is ignored with a one-time warning. The root carries the module's
top-level annotation. The version decision lives in the CUDA backend, so the
backend-neutral pass and thunk do not depend on stream_executor/cuda.

CommandExecutor pushes one ScopedCommandBufferAnnotation per command with the
lazy constructor, so the per-command annotation string
(GetInstructionAnnotationString, sharing GetInstructionAnnotation's lookup) is
only built while recording is on. Adds GetCurrentModuleAnnotations() to
annotation.h.

display_title: [XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

When `xla.apply_indexing` has a result expression that simplifies to a bare input variable (`SymbolicExprType::kVariable`), `ApplyIndexingOp::fold` and `FoldApplyIndexingOperands` previously folded it directly to the operand SSA value even when the `xla.apply_indexing` op (or its constrained `IndexingMap` domain) carried a strictly tighter `xla.range` than `GetRange(operand)`. Similarly, `emitters::ApplyIndexing` immediately called `createOrFold<ApplyIndexingOp>`, discarding narrowed domain bounds whenever a constrained sub-map simplified to an identity variable.

Teach `ApplyIndexingOp::fold` and `FoldApplyIndexingOperands` to retain `xla.apply_indexing` when folding to an operand would lose a tighter `xla.range` annotation on the op, and add an opt-in `preserve_result_ranges` parameter to `emitters::ApplyIndexing` so callers with trusted domain constraints can materialize an unfolded single-result `ApplyIndexingOp` carrying `xla.range` when a `kVariable` result narrows `GetRange(operand)`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use xla::GetRange and unit divisors in Triton mask elision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use xla::GetRange and unit divisors in Triton mask elision.

Triton tile mask elision previously inspected only `arith.constant` and `xla.apply_indexing` ops directly in `IsGuaranteedInBounds`, missing `xla.range` attributes on values such as kernel `pid` casts or folded indexing operands, and did not short-circuit `divisor == 1` in `IsGuaranteedDivisible` for arbitrary dynamic `mlir::Value` offsets. In addition, `XTileEntryToTriton` dropped the `xla.range` attribute from `xtile.entry_func`'s tile ID argument when lowering to `tt.get_program_id` + `arith.index_cast`, and neither `IsGuaranteedInBounds` nor `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass` guarded against infeasible intervals or signed `int64_t` overflow when checking strided tile bounds.

Query `xla::GetRange` in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass` with explicit feasibility and overflow-safe strided bounds checks (`min_delta` / `max_delta`), treat `divisor == 1` as trivially divisible in `IsGuaranteedDivisible`, and forward `xtile.entry_func`'s tile ID `xla.range` attribute onto the lowered `arith.index_cast` in `XTileEntryToTriton`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use 64-bit dimensions in CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm.

`CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm` in `xla/service/cpu/dot_op_emitter.cc` narrowed the
GEMM dimensions `m`, `k`, and `n` from `int64_t` to 32-bit `int` before
checking `small_gemm` upper bounds. When multi-threaded Eigen is disabled,
dimensions `>= 2^31` that wrap negative in 32-bit `int` or dimensions `> 2^32`
that wrap modulo `2^32` into `<= 128` misclassified giant GEMMs as
`DotImplementationStrategy::kTiledLlvmIrGemm` instead of `kEigen`, allowing
`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass` to treat them as inlineable small GEMMs.

Widen `m`, `k`, and `n` to `int64_t` in `CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm`, and add
symbolic HLO unit tests in
`xla/service/cpu/small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test.cc`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use 64-bit dimensions in CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm.

`CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm` in `xla/service/cpu/dot_op_emitter.cc` narrowed the
GEMM dimensions `m`, `k`, and `n` from `int64_t` to 32-bit `int` before
checking `small_gemm` upper bounds. When multi-threaded Eigen is disabled,
dimensions `>= 2^31` that wrap negative in 32-bit `int` or dimensions `> 2^32`
that wrap modulo `2^32` into `<= 128` misclassified giant GEMMs as
`DotImplementationStrategy::kTiledLlvmIrGemm` instead of `kEigen`, allowing
`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass` to treat them as inlineable small GEMMs.

Widen `m`, `k`, and `n` to `int64_t` in `CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm`, and add
symbolic HLO unit tests in
`xla/service/cpu/small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test.cc`.

display_title: [XLA] Check dimension indexes before use in HloEvaluator

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check dimension indexes before use in HloEvaluator

HloEvaluator::HandleSort reads key_shape.dimensions(sort_dim) one line
before the TF_RET_CHECK that bounds sort_dim. HloVerifier only checks
the upper bound of the sort dimension, so this read also happens for
verified modules with a negative sort dimension. Move the check before
the read.

HandleBroadcast, HandleScan and HandleSetDimensionSize use an
instruction-supplied dimension to index a shape's dimensions without a
bounds check. HandleScan also writes start[scan_dim] and
slab_dims[scan_dim], where both vectors are sized by the operand or
result rank. Return an error when the dimension is out of range.

Add regression tests for each case and boundary-value controls.

Add two OpInterfaces in `ifrt/ir/ifrt_interfaces.td` to unify array/control operand and result access across IFRT operations:
1. `IfrtArrayOpInterface` (attached to `ReshardOp`, `CopyArraysOp`, `BitcastArraysOp`, `RemapArraysOp`, `CallOp`, and `CallLoadedExecutableOp`), exposing `getInputs()`, `getInputsMutable()`, `getOutputs()`, `getControlInputs()`, `getControlInputsMutable()`, and `getControlOutput()`.
2. `IfrtPairwiseArrayOpInterface` (inheriting `IfrtArrayOpInterface`, attached to `ReshardOp`, `CopyArraysOp`, and `BitcastArraysOp`), exposing `getDonated()`, `getInputForOutput()`, `cloneWithKeptOutputs()`, and `replaceWithKeptOutputs()`.

Also extract a pure-MLIR `IfrtIrTestBase` (`ifrt_ir_test_base.{h,cc}`) with `mlir_context_`, dialect registration, and `LoadFromSource` as the base of `IfrtIrLoadedExecutableTestBase` and `IfrtInterfacesTest`.

display_title: Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support.

Official Linux wheels are now built with Clang and `libc++` instead of `libstdc++` , and introduce Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels. Out-of-tree C++ custom ops targeting official Linux wheels must be compiled with Clang and `-stdlib=libc++` (now returned automatically by `tf.sysconfig.get_compile_flags()`).

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). display_title: [PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

head_commit.message:
[PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

When executing CPU computations, PJRT and XLA thread pools configure the CPU to flush subnormal floating-point numbers to zero to improve performance. However, when XLA calls back into Python (via `jax.pure_callback`, `io_callback`, or `buffer_callback`), this setting was left enabled on the calling thread. Python code (like NumPy) expects standard floating-point behavior, so leaving this setting enabled caused subnormal numbers to silently become zero inside user callbacks.

This change adds `tsl::port::ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and `tsl::port::ScopedSetRound(FE_TONEAREST)` to `xla::HostCallbackScope`. This ensures all Python callbacks run with standard floating-point settings, and safely restores XLA's expected settings when the callback returns.

Bumps `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 85 and adds regression tests guarded by this version.

head_commit.message:
In `PartitionConvolutionTiledOutput`, `ReshardAsWindowedInput` runs on `lhs` and returns `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` ordered by `lhs` dimensions. When a base dilated convolution has permuted spatial and feature or batch dimensions between `lhs` and the output (such as `b0f_0io->bf0` after `TransposeFolding` or `01fb_01io->b01f`) and requires a per shard output window alignment slice, passing `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` directly to `CreateDynamicSlice` on `sharded_conv` applies the spatial slice offset to the wrong output dimension.

Map `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` from `lhs` dimension order into output dimension order via `input_to_output_indices` before creating the `dynamic-slice` on `sharded_conv`. Existing programs whose `lhs` and output dimensions have identical ordering or do not emit an output alignment slice do not change behavior, with no flag.

display_title: Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

head_commit.message:
Restrict hwloc topology discovery in `numa_hwloc.cc` to NUMA and CPU objects.

By default, `GetHWLocTopology()` in `numa_hwloc.cc` loads the full machine hardware hierarchy—including CPU cache levels, PCI/OS I/O devices (`linuxio`), and per-core `x86` CPUID probing—even though TSL's NUMA utilities only ever query `HWLOC_OBJ_NUMANODE` and CPU affinity sets. On large multi-socket / high-core-count hosts, this redundant discovery adds unnecessary sysfs traversal and CPUID probing overhead during NUMA initialization. This change configures `HWLOC_TYPE_FILTER_KEEP_NONE` and excludes the `linuxio` and `x86` discovery components before `hwloc_topology_load()` so hwloc only discovers the NUMA node and CPU sets that TSL uses.

head_commit.message:
Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

When `PjRtCApiCompiler::Compile` or `PjRtCApiPhaseCompiler::CompileToRelocatable` is called for ahead-of-time compilation without a live `PjRtClient` (`client == nullptr`), program serialization previously could not query `client->plugin_attributes()` and fell back to the default 12-week compatibility StableHLO and Shardy versions (`xla::GetDefaultStablehloVersion()` and `xla::GetDefaultSdyVersion()`).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optionally register host memory in a shared CUDA context.

`cuMemHostUnregister` synchronizes the context that the memory was registered in while holding that context's lock: it waits for all of the context's streams, and other threads can't launch work or enqueue copies in the context meanwhile. With memory registered in a device's primary context, this can deadlock with an in-flight collective. The device's side of the collective is already enqueued, but the peer can't launch its side until a copy that has to be enqueued in the same primary context is enqueued, and that copy waits for the context lock held by `cuMemHostUnregister`.

With `XLA_CUDA_REGISTER_HOST_MEMORY_IN_SHARED_CONTEXT=1`, `CudaExecutor::HostMemoryRegister`/`HostMemoryUnregister` register and unregister host memory in one context shared by all executors in the process instead of the executor's primary context:

- The env var is read and the shared context is created on the first registration, on the device of the executor doing it, and the context lives until the process exits. In PjRt that is always the client's first device, since `DmaMap` and the pinned host memory allocator register through it; the device only determines which GPU holds the context's memory. It's created with `cuCtxCreate_v4` (same signature in CUDA 12 and 13 headers; needs a 12.5+ driver), with the stack size limit set to 0 since no kernels run in it. If it can't be created, every executor registers in its primary context.
- It has no streams, so unregistering memory registered in it waits for nothing and doesn't block any primary context, whichever context the caller has current. The memory is registered as portable, so it's still treated as pinned by every context, and one shared context is enough for all devices.
- Registration pushes the shared context on top of the activated primary context and pops it afterwards, so the calling thread is left in the same state as without the flag.
- Unregistering no longer implicitly waits for work in the registering device's primary context. It never waited for work on other devices, so callers must already make sure the memory is no longer used before unregistering it.

The shared context costs a few hundred MiB of device memory, so the flag is off by default.

Adds `cuCtxCreate_v4` to `cuda.symbols`.

buffers before running. All three did this only in `ExecuteOnStream`, via
`stream->MemZero`. Their `Record` paths built argument addresses and then
created exactly one node with nothing in between, so once a thunk was captured
into a command buffer the zeroing was absent from the recorded graph entirely.
`CuDnnThunk` missed it on both branches: the explicit path never zeroed, and the
traced fallback traces only `graph->Execute(...)`, leaving the `MemZero` outside
the captured lambda.

`Record` now records a memset command per zeroed buffer and makes the thunk's own
command depend on them, so ordering is transitively unchanged for anything
downstream. Because buffer addresses move between executions, the memsets must be
updated too, and `Record` is handed back only the single node it returned — so
the memset handles are kept in `CommandStateManager`, keyed by the node they were
recorded alongside. That keying matters: an unrolled while loop records one
command into the same command buffer once per trip, and all those recordings
share a single state object. `CustomCallThunk` and `RaggedAllToAllThunk` use the
same pattern.

The shared logic lives in a new `zeroed_outputs.{h,cc}`. No signature, proto or
emitter changes, and no change to the eager path.

🎯 Justification

This is the default path. `kKernel`/`kCustomKernel` map to `FUSION` and `kCuDnn`
to `CUDNN`, both enabled by default, and `IsConvertible` has no zeroed-outputs
guard. Any Triton/Pallas kernel declaring `zeroed_outputs`, and cuDNN fMHA via
`should_memzero`, silently loses its zeroing once a command buffer forms.

Kernels request zeroed outputs because they accumulate into them rather than
overwriting, and a command buffer replays the same buffers every step, so the
error compounds across iterations. Failure is silent without any error, just a missing
node.

This looks to have been introduced by commit [604cf9e4c0](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/37025), which added `zeroed_output_buffer_indices_` touching
only `ExecuteOnStream`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A — correctness fix, no performance claim

🧪 Unit Tests:

**`kernel_thunk_test.cc`, `custom_kernel_thunk_test.cc`** — a test
kernel computes `c = a + b` with `a=1, b=2`. These tests zero **`b`**, an input;
zeroing the output `c` proves nothing since the kernel overwrites it. Zeroing
recorded gives `c == 1`, dropped gives `c == 3`.
- `ExecuteOnStreamZeroed` — eager control
- `RecordCommandBufferZeroed`, `RecordCommandBufferUpdateZeroed`
- `RecordCommandBufferTwoRecordingsZeroed` (kernel only) — one thunk recorded
  twice into one command buffer, both updated against moved buffers. This is the
  unrolled-loop shape; a flat memset list leaves the first recording stale.

**`cudnn_thunk_test.cc`** — a probe output the graph never writes, pre-filled
with `0xdeadbeef`: zeroed reads 0, dropped reads the sentinel.
`CuDnnThunkZeroedTest.{ExecuteOnStream, RecordCreateReplayAndUpdate}`,
parameterized over the explicit and traced branches — both fail without the fix,
for different reasons.

Verified both ways: all pass with the fix; with the three `Record` bodies
reverted, the eager controls still pass and every `Record*` case fails.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. The thunk-level tests exercise both record paths and the
create/update cycle directly, including the cuDNN explicit and traced branches.

head_commit.message:
Upgrade XLA's Bazel `@hwloc` dependency from 2.7.1 to 2.13.0.

XLA's Bazel workspace (`hwloc/workspace.bzl`) was pinned to `hwloc 2.7.1` (from 2022), missing years of upstream topology fixes and performance improvements. In particular, `hwloc 2.7.1` reads Linux `/sys` topology files via stdio `fopen`/`fgets`/`fclose` (allocating and freeing a heap buffer per file during `hwloc_topology_load`), whereas `hwloc 2.13.0` uses stack-buffered `openat`/`read`/`close` (`hwloc_read_path_by_length`), significantly reducing syscall and allocator overhead during NUMA topology initialization.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rewrite batched one-hot dots and one-hot reductions to gather.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rewrite batched one-hot dots and one-hot reductions to gather.

***Problem:*** `DotStrengthReduction` only rewrites unbatched one-hot `dot`s to `gather`, so batched one-hot `dot`s and 1-D one-hot masked sum reductions (`reduce_sum(select(idx == iota, x, 0))`) still scan all `K` elements to read a single value.

***Solution:*** Share a one-hot lowering that emits a single-slice `gather` guarded by an in-bounds `select` (keeping zero outputs for out-of-range indices) and use it in `DotStrengthReduction` for batched one-hot `dot`s and in `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` for 1-D one-hot `reduce_sum`s, peeling `broadcast` and up to one widening `convert` so the gather reads the narrow operand directly.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013355786

name: CI ROCm
display_title: #HloDiff Ignore parameter names when signature-matching called computations.

head_commit.message:
#HloDiff Ignore parameter names when signature-matching called computations.

`MatchCallGraphs` phase 3 groups unmatched callees by caller opcode, op_name and
`ComputeProgramShape(include_ids=false).ToString()`. That string includes the
parameter names (minus the id suffix), so callees whose parameters are named
differently, e.g. `Arg_0` vs `p0`, are never signature-matched, even though
parameter names aren't part of the signature.

When the callees are left unmapped, the computation graph matcher doesn't
anchor their parameters and roots, and the exact subgraph matcher maps
identical duplicated computations (e.g. two copies of `log_softmax`) crosswise.

On a synthetic mutator pair (46k instructions, 34 mutations + rename) this
removes the remaining 52 wrong mappings; mapping precision/recall goes from
0.9989 to 1.0.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013336140

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

One hipGraphLaunch yields many kernel-dispatch records under one correlation
id. ApiActivityInfoExchange copied the kernel_info of the first record to
arrive onto the HIP API row, then copied that back onto every activity kernel
row with the same correlation id. So every kernel in a graph launch showed the
registers, shared memory, grid and block of whichever record reached the
buffer first.

Two more cases went through the same copy. kernel_info and memcpy_info share a
union, so when a memcpy record arrived first, every kernel row showed the
copy's bytes read as kernel details. And a copy API served by a blit kernel
gave that kernel a zero grid and block, because the API row only received the
first 16 bytes of the kernel's details.

KernelEvent already fills each activity row's kernel_info from its own
dispatch record and code-object symbol, and kernel_details is exported only
for activity kernel rows, so the activity loop no longer overwrites it. The
API loop no longer copies kernel_info onto the HIP API row either: that row
does not export it, and the first record may not be a kernel, in which case
the copy read a memcpy's bytes as KernelDetails. The host row still takes
device_id and stream_id from the first record. The activity loop's Memset case
no longer copies memset_info from the API row, which never carries it; the
tracer emits no Memset activities today, so this changes nothing yet.

MultipleActivitiesPerCorrelationIdAllExported now gives its three kernels
distinct grids and checks that each exported row keeps its own.
TestAddKernelEventAndExport now initialises its activity's kernel_info,
which it used to export uninitialised. Both exchange tests stop setting
kernel details on the HIP API event: those never reached the output, and the
API row now carries none.

display_title: Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

display_title: Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

head_commit.message:
Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

When `PjRtCApiCompiler::Compile` or `PjRtCApiPhaseCompiler::CompileToRelocatable` is called for ahead-of-time compilation without a live `PjRtClient` (`client == nullptr`), program serialization previously could not query `client->plugin_attributes()` and fell back to the default 12-week compatibility StableHLO and Shardy versions (`xla::GetDefaultStablehloVersion()` and `xla::GetDefaultSdyVersion()`).

Because `PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` is a plugin-level C API call on `const PJRT_Api*` that does not require a `PJRT_Client*`, fall back to querying `c_api->PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` when `client == nullptr` (or when the client does not report attributes) so ahead-of-time compilation serializes programs using the plugin's actual `stablehlo_current_version` and `sdy_current_version`.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

In single-replica SPMD (`replica_count == 1 && num_partitions > 1`), `replica-id()` is always 0, so the flattened device ID (`replica-id() * num_partitions + partition-id()`) simplifies directly to `partition-id()`. Previously, collective decomposition only folded `replica-id()` to 0 for cross-replica-and-partition groups (emitted by GSPMD), leaving a redundant `replica-id()` multiply-add for flattened-ID groups (emitted by Shardy). Also propagate layouts to all newly created index instructions when decomposing collectives after layout assignment.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

When decomposing `all-gather` or `reduce-scatter` with `COLLECTIVE_OP_GROUP_MODE_FLATTENED_ID` in a single-replica SPMD module (`replica_count == 1 && num_partitions > 1`), `replica-id()` is always zero, so the global device ID is equal to `partition-id()` directly rather than `replica-id() * num_partitions + partition-id()`. display_title: [XLA] Reject index_vector_dim batching dims in gather/scatter expansion

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject index_vector_dim batching dims in gather/scatter expansion

ExpandIndexVectorIntoOperandSpace builds one index per explicit
batching dim of the gather or scatter indices.
GenerateExplicitBatchDimIndices skips index_vector_dim, so when
start_indices_batching_dims (or scatter_indices_batching_dims)
contains index_vector_dim, the matching entry stays null and is passed
to MakeBroadcastHlo, which dereferences it. HloVerifier accepts such
modules, both with an explicit index_vector_dim and with the implicit
trailing one.

Return InvalidArgument in that case. Add GatherExpander and
ScatterExpander tests for both cases, plus controls with the batching
dim next to index_vector_dim.

display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced incorrect results on GPU compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` exponentiation-by-squaring loop upper bound from 6 to the integer element bit-width so all exponent bits are processed.

Fixes #118202

display_title: `xla::CompileOptions` is copied by value across compilation, caching, and serialization boundaries, while `multi_slice_config` was stored as an unowned raw pointer. Callers and executables had to maintain separate sidecar holders to keep the configuration alive, and cached compiled executables could retain a dangling pointer once the caller's `MultiSliceConfig` was destroyed.

head_commit.message:
`xla::CompileOptions` is copied by value across compilation, caching, and serialization boundaries, while `multi_slice_config` was stored as an unowned raw pointer. Callers and executables had to maintain separate sidecar holders to keep the configuration alive, and cached compiled executables could retain a dangling pointer once the caller's `MultiSliceConfig` was destroyed.

Changing `xla::CompileOptions::multi_slice_config` to `std::shared_ptr<const MultiSliceConfig>` gives `CompileOptions` shared ownership of the configuration across copies and throughout an executable's lifetime, while keeping `LoadOptions::multi_slice_config` and `ExecuteOptions::multi_slice_config` as non-owning pointers for synchronous calls.

Migration guideline:
* Populating `CompileOptions::multi_slice_config`: Assign or move a `std::shared_ptr<const MultiSliceConfig>` or `std::unique_ptr<const MultiSliceConfig>` instead of a raw `.get()` pointer.
* Passing `CompileOptions::multi_slice_config` to non-owning APIs (such as `LoadOptions`, `ExecuteOptions`, or `GetDefaultDeviceAssignment`): Pass `compile_options.multi_slice_config.get()`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013157910

display_title: Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

head_commit.message:
Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

When `PjRtCApiCompiler::Compile` is called for ahead-of-time compilation without a live `PjRtClient` (`client == nullptr`), `SerializeProgram` previously could not query `client->plugin_attributes()` and fell back to the default 12-week compatibility StableHLO and Shardy versions (`xla::GetDefaultStablehloVersion()` and `xla::GetDefaultSdyVersion()`).

Because `PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` is a plugin-level C API call on `const PJRT_Api*` that does not require a `PJRT_Client*`, fall back to querying `c_api->PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` when `client == nullptr` (or when the client does not report attributes) so ahead-of-time compilation serializes programs using the plugin's actual `stablehlo_current_version` and `sdy_current_version`.

display_title: Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables building and testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

display_title: Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

head_commit.message:
Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

Adds protocol version 28 and a new IfrtRequest/IfrtResponse pair so a client
can load a serialized executable on the server backend.

Client: Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable uploads the bytes through the
host buffer store, sends the request, and builds the executable from the
CompileResponse. It returns Unimplemented if the server is older than
version 28, and rejects host callbacks.

Server: IfrtBackend handles the request on the compile thread pool, waits for
the uploaded bytes, calls the default Compiler, and returns the same
CompileResponse as Compile. The Compile response code is now shared.

The previous Unimplemented error cited an unstable serialization format. That is
not a concern here: the proxy never reads the bytes and sends them unchanged.
The server backend that loads them checks that they match its own runtime and
returns an error status if they do not. The same compatibility rule applies to
any IFRT client that loads a serialized executable.

On systems without CUDA drivers (e.g. CPU-only workstations or containers), attempting to dynamically load the CUDA runtime DSO fails as expected. display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.
Copybara import of the project:

--
9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

--
305022f3c7322f0cd593997b81715ea9ed473d15 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Bail out of the trivial reduce-window rewrite for any dynamic operand with a crop

The slice that applies a negative window padding covers every dimension of
the operand, so a dynamic dimension without a crop still breaks it. Check the
whole operand shape once before slicing instead of only the cropped dimension.

Merging this change closes #48875

display_title: Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

head_commit.message:
Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

When a second client connects to an IFRT proxy server that only supports a single active client, the server terminates the session with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Only one client can connect via the proxy server at a time.`. Previously, `GrpcClientSession` could overwrite this status with `CANCELLED` (by calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` even when `ReadLoop()` had already exited) or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (if `Finish()` completed before `Enqueue()`).

Avoid calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` when `ReadLoop()` has already exited, and store the final session status in `finish_status_` so subsequent `Enqueue()` calls return it.

On systems without CUDA drivers (e.g. CPU-only workstations or containers), attempting to dynamically load the CUDA runtime DSO fails as expected. Logging this at INFO causes noisy STDERR output upon importing TensorFlow (including "WARNING: All log messages before absl::InitializeLog() is called are written to STDERR" and "Could not find cuda drivers on your machine, GPU will not be used").

Demoting this log to VLOG(1) prevents unwanted STDERR noise on default verbosity while retaining diagnostic output when verbosity is explicitly requested (e.g. via TF_CPP_MAX_VLOG_LEVEL=1).

display_title: [XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleDynamicSlice`
(`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), folding a
1D `dynamic-slice` of an `iota` (or scaled `iota`) clamps the scalar
`S32`/`U32` start index to `[0, iota_size - 1]` by narrowing
`iota_size - 1` directly to `int32_t` or `uint32_t`. When
`iota_size - 1` exceeds `INT32_MAX` (for `S32` indices) or `UINT32_MAX`
(for `U32` indices), the upper bound wraps around and corrupts the
clamped index.

Saturate the clamp upper bound to the maximum representable value of
`index_type`, which is equivalent across all 32-bit index values, and
add symbolic >32-bit `S32` and `U32` unit tests.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012198883

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

--
305022f3c7322f0cd593997b81715ea9ed473d15 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Bail out of the trivial reduce-window rewrite for any dynamic operand with a crop

The slice that applies a negative window padding covers every dimension of
the operand, so a dynamic dimension without a crop still breaks it. Check the
whole operand shape once before slicing instead of only the cropped dimension.

Merging this change closes #48875
