display_title: Support cross-memory-kind donation and mark donated buffers deleted in PjRtArray.

head_commit.message:
Support cross-memory-kind donation and mark donated buffers deleted in PjRtArray.

Previously, `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` rejected `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` when copying across different memory kinds with an `Unimplemented` error, left the source array's `PjRtBuffer` pointer intact when donating on the same device and memory kind, and did not call `PjRtBuffer::Delete()` on the source buffer when donating across devices or memory spaces. In addition, several `PjRtArray` methods assumed elements of `pjrt_buffers_` were non-null even after cross-device donation set `pjrt_buffers_[index] = nullptr`.

Allow `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` across different memory spaces in `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` by deleting and clearing the source `PjRtBuffer` after `CopyToMemorySpace` initiates the transfer, and move `pjrt_buffers_[index]` when donating on the same device and memory kind so the source `PjRtArray` is marked deleted. Guard against null donated buffer slots in `CopySinglePjRtBuffer`, `CopyImpl`, `CopyToHostBuffer`, `GetReadyFuture`, and debug checks in `pjrt_layout`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004877589

display_title: Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

head_commit.message:
Query plugin attributes from PJRT_Api when compiling without a client.

When `PjRtCApiCompiler::Compile` is called for ahead-of-time compilation without a live `PjRtClient` (`client == nullptr`), `SerializeProgram` previously could not query `client->plugin_attributes()` and fell back to the default 12-week compatibility StableHLO and Shardy versions (`xla::GetDefaultStablehloVersion()` and `xla::GetDefaultSdyVersion()`).

Because `PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` is a plugin-level C API call on `const PJRT_Api*` that does not require a `PJRT_Client*`, fall back to querying `c_api->PJRT_Plugin_Attributes` when `client == nullptr` (or when the client does not report attributes) so ahead-of-time compilation serializes programs using the plugin's actual `stablehlo_current_version` and `sdy_current_version`.

display_title: Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

head_commit.message:
Propagate IFRT proxy server RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error to client.

When a second client connects to an IFRT proxy server that only supports a single active client, the server terminates the session with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Only one client can connect via the proxy server at a time.`. Previously, `GrpcClientSession` could overwrite this status with `CANCELLED` (by calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` even when `ReadLoop()` had already exited) or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (if `Finish()` completed before `Enqueue()`).

Avoid calling `context_->TryCancel()` before `stream_->Finish()` when `ReadLoop()` has already exited, and store the final session status in `finish_status_` so subsequent `Enqueue()` calls return it.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009283529

display_title: Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Batch output buffer allocations per memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

Dispatching executables with thousands of outputs currently calls `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` and `GetOnDeviceBytesCount` once per non-aliased output leaf, while `use_output_arena` couples all output buffer lifetimes to the longest-lived output buffer.

Add `PjRtRawClient::AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` (with a default implementation delegating to `AllocateRawBufferForExecute` so existing backends such as GPU and CPU preserve their current behavior), cache static output leaf buffer sizes in `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::output_buffer_sizes_in_bytes_`, and dispatch one `AllocateRawBuffersForExecute` call per memory space in `CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` when `use_output_arena` is disabled.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012864654

display_title: Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Group output buffer allocations by memory space in CommonPjRtClient.

`CommonPjRtClient::AllocateOutputBuffersWithInputReuse` currently scans `device->memory_spaces()` on every non-aliased output leaf, allocates non-arena buffers inline during the loop, and collects arena allocations into an unordered pointer-keyed `absl::flat_hash_map<PjRtMemorySpace*, ...>`. Preparing for per-memory-space batched output allocation requires deterministic grouping of pending output allocations across both the default and arena paths.

Collect non-aliased output allocations into an `absl::InlinedVector` ordered deterministically by first-seen memory space `kind_id`, resolving `PjRtMemorySpace*` once per distinct `kind_id`, and execute either the per-output or arena allocation loop over those grouped entries with no functional change.

When CUPTI V2 multi-subscriber mode (`allowMultipleSubscribers = 1`) is active (such as in CUDA 13.4 static CUPTI builds), enabling `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` via `cuptiActivityEnable_v2` returns `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` unless the global `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_MULTI_SUBSCRIBER_GRAPH_TRACE` (`20`) attribute is set to `1` before enabling any activity kinds.

Set `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_ATTR_ENABLE_MULTI_SUBSCRIBER_GRAPH_TRACE` to `1` in `CuptiTracer::EnableActivityTracing` before calling `ActivityEnableV2` when `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` is selected, and reset it to `0` in `CuptiTracer::DisableActivityTracing` after disabling activity kinds so subsequent node-level graph tracing sessions continue to receive per-node records. Also allow `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` and `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_COMPATIBLE` in `CuptiErrorManager::ActivitySetAttributeV2`.

display_title: [PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

head_commit.message:
[PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

When executing CPU computations, PJRT and XLA thread pools configure the CPU to flush subnormal floating-point numbers to zero to improve performance. However, when XLA calls back into Python (via `jax.pure_callback`, `io_callback`, or `buffer_callback`), this setting was left enabled on the calling thread. Python code (like NumPy) expects standard floating-point behavior, so leaving this setting enabled caused subnormal numbers to silently become zero inside user callbacks.

This change adds `tsl::port::ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and `tsl::port::ScopedSetRound(FE_TONEAREST)` to `xla::HostCallbackScope`. This ensures all Python callbacks run with standard floating-point settings, and safely restores XLA's expected settings when the callback returns.

Bumps `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 84 and adds regression tests guarded by this version.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012993070

head_commit.message:
PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

🎯 Justification
`ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper` creates async computations on the parallel execution thread, while `SanitizeConstantNames` previously ran only on the main execution thread.

As a result, constants in these async computations could reach GPU code generation with unsanitized names and trigger the ConstantNameToGlobalName DCHECK.

This change runs constant-name sanitization across all execution threads while keeping the remaining post-scheduling passes scoped to the main execution thread.

Fixes #50829

display_title: Fix 32-bit overflows in SPMD pad-with-wrap and iota partitioning

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit overflows in SPMD pad-with-wrap and iota partitioning

Fix three >32-bit dimension bugs in `xla/service/spmd/spmd_partitioner.cc`:
1. In `SpmdPartitioner::PreprocessHlos`, widen `rotate_lhs_amount` from `int`
   to `int64_t` and use `U64` (instead of `U32`) for the merge `iota` and
   `select` limit constants when `padded_size > UINT32_MAX`.
2. When `padded_size > INT32_MAX`, guard the pad-with-wrap rewrite on matching
   even shardings for `mid` and `hlo` and bounded halo size so uneven sharding
   or large halos fall back to standard `kConcatenate` partitioning instead of
   hitting 32-bit helpers.
3. In `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleIota`, compute shard offsets in 64-bit
   (`U64` for `U64` iota, `S64` otherwise) whenever `shard_dim > INT32_MAX` or
   `(num_shards - 1) * shard_dim > INT32_MAX`, preserving the `S32` path for
   smaller shapes.

display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on `multiProcessorCount`, so aot plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we plumb the compile-time `GpuTargetConfig` from `GpuExecutable` (`gpu_topology_`) into `Thunk::InitializeParams`, extract the target SM count in `CuDnnThunk`, and pass it to `DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`. When that target SM count is lower than the attached GPU's, `CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` builds `DeviceProperties` from the live `DeviceDescription` with `core_count` lowered to match (keeping all other hardware properties from the live GPU for validation) and runs warmup on the handle.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013012065

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` multiplied the per-tile coalescing
utilization rate by the transfer-size HBM derate on dot fusions, compounding
both penalties on small GEMMs into an unrealistically low effective bandwidth.
Take the minimum of the two rates instead and apply it in floating point.

In addition, when a fused prologue widens narrow inputs (such as `s8 -> bf16`),
counting only fusion parameter reads under-estimates K-loop L2 traffic by 2x
and causes slow widening fusions to beat cuBLASLt. Bound L2 traffic below by
the masked dot-operand tile reads across the K-loop.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO with buffer assignment after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes, and `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` accepts `HloModule*` without `buffer_assignment`. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers both the scheduled `HloModule` and `BufferAssignmentProto` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses` and attaches `BufferAssignmentProto`, the `HloProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule`, post-scheduling transformations, and `buffer_assignment` present in the `HloProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Change `SymbolUploader::MaybeUploadOptimizedHloModule` to accept `const HloProto&` and pass both `MakeHloProto(module)` and `gpu_executable->buffer_assignment_proto()` into `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Store the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedHloModule` directly on `HloModule` (preserved across `HloModule::Clone`) and read it inside `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping.
- Return the previous `std::unique_ptr<SymbolUploader>` from `SymbolUploaderRegistry::Register` so `ScopedSymbolUploader` restores the previous uploader on destruction.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloWithBufferAssignmentAfterRunBackend` using `tsl::DeterministicProtoHash64` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloProto` with `buffer_assignment` (even after `HloModule::Clone`) and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (or with `embed_hlo_module = false`) do not produce an embedded backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule, post-scheduling changes, and `buffer_assignment` before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling and memory analysis consumers require the final scheduled `HloProto` and `BufferAssignmentProto` that execute on the GPU.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013010631

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Account for element type bit width when estimating register usage.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Account for element type bit width when estimating register usage.

Previously, register usage estimation assumed one register per element regardless of the element type. 64-bit types take two 32-bit register. Sub-32-bit types are stored unpacked with one value per register.
